text.tspan: Protectli Vault V1410. WAN, VLAN gateways,
DHCP, DNS, NAT, firewall policy, VPN, and
Core managed switch: 8x 2.5GbE PoE+ ports, 2x 10G SFP+
uplinks, 802.1Q VLANs, trunk/access ports, ACLs, and
Switch Port 2: trunk + PoE+. Each SSID maps
OPNsense routes between VLANs, but inter-VLAN traffic is
blocked unless a specific firewall rule allows it.
i9-13900HK, 32GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, one Ethernet port. Switch
Port 3 is a trunk carrying server-facing VLANs.
NGINX reverse proxy and Nextcloud Server public app path. WAN
Jellyfin Server, storage, backups, and database/backend services
Wazuh manager, indexer, dashboard, agents, syslog, and file
Omada Controller container if hosted on the NucBox. Admin access
Public HTTPS path: WAN → OPNsense NAT → NGINX reverse proxy → Nextcloud/Jellyfin backends
Logs and security events flow to Wazuh
Logical VLAN Zones — traffic between zones is controlled by OPNsense firewall rules
• Only TCP 443 from WAN should be forwarded to the DMZ NGINX reverse proxy. Avoid direct public exposure of Nextcloud or Jellyfin
• The NucBox uses one Ethernet connection as a trunk. Use Linux VLAN subinterfaces and Docker networks, or document simpler Docker
• The safest remote administration path is WireGuard VPN into OPNsense. Do not expose management dashboards directly to the
• Forward OPNsense, NGINX, Nextcloud, Jellyfin, Docker, Linux auth, and FIM events into Wazuh for evidence and portfolio
• Use split DNS / host overrides so internal devices reach cloud.yourdomain.com and media.yourdomain.com cleanly.
Solid arrow = physical or routed network path
Dashed arrow = public service or log/event flow
SOC = Wazuh monitoring and evidence collection
VLAN 99 = disabled/parking network for unused ports
